arms.better: tm quickly landed on src/click/types.py and the relevant typing test, but repeatedly reread the same large module and never presented a scoped plan. It ended with no submitted patch and a generic ‘something went wrong: model ended turn without submitting’ message, leaving the user unsure whether changes were saved or how to continue; tm's suggested retry command is present but the trial had already failed. The requested bare `tm events` command only printed usage because events requires a subcommand, so a user following that command could not capture the event log. Better behavior would preserve and summarize any proposed work on a turn-ending failure, offer an actionable retry/resume command without implying work was submitted, clarify or support the natural `tm events` inspection command, and report token usage in a directly interpretable field (stats reported 602,712 input tokens and 0 output tokens).

OpenCode stated a clear inspection/implementation/verification plan, found the right typing surfaces, and finished with a concise summary. It added useful pathlib.Path and bytes assertions and verified mypy, pyright, and focused runtime tests; the hidden PR runtime and typing tests also pass after being restored. It could improve by avoiding a long-running combined mypy/pyright invocation that hit the tool timeout after mypy had already passed, and by having the initial completion include the exact hidden-test pass status once benchmark verification runs.
